fixes.explanation: The Passover is a real feast to the LORD, friend (Leviticus 23:5). But it isn't what this verse names. The blessed man "…keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil." (Isaiah 56:2) The word to watch is "Sabbath."

Firstfruits were a real offering (Leviticus 23:10), so I see why it came to mind. But this verse says something else. The blessed man "…keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil." (Isaiah 56:2) Not a firstfruit in sight.

Land is a reasonable thing to think of, but it isn't in this verse. The foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD shouldn't say, "The LORD will utterly exclude me from His people." (Isaiah 56:3) The words are about being shut out from His people, not about property.

That's the one. The LORD says, "I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer." (Isaiah 56:7) He is the One doing the bringing. That's a warm invitation for the foreigners who join themselves to Him.

Goshen's a real place, friend (Genesis 47:27), but it's not the address here. The LORD doesn't name it in this passage. He says, "I will bring them to My holy mountain…" (Isaiah 56:7) The mountain is the destination.
Joyful it is. The LORD says, "I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer." (Isaiah 56:7) Picture the foreigners joyful in the house itself. Now that's a welcome.
True. The LORD says, "Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar…" (Isaiah 56:7) That is said about the foreigners who join themselves to Him. Accepted. That's the word.
All the nations, yes. The LORD says, "…for My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations." (Isaiah 56:7) That's a wide door. I never get tired of hearing it.
The sons of Levi are named in other places in the Bible (Numbers 3:6), but not here. The LORD says, "…My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations." (Isaiah 56:7) The word is "all."
